data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --partition cpulong
#   --nodes 1
#   --ntasks-per-node 1
#   --mem-per-cpu 8G
#   --time 3-0:00:00
#   --job-name sweep
#   --output slogs/sweep-%J.log

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --time=72h \
  --queue=cpulong \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p slogs

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu 8G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name sweep is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: Slurm output naming uses %J; Flux has no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but log naming/organization may be degraded.
# Best-effort: use Flux job id.
exec >"slogs/sweep-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.log" 2>&1

module purge

singularity exec ${OPENSPIEL_IMG} wandb agent ${WANDB_PROJECT}
'
"
}
